title: Worms?
tagline: Teach your worm, then watch what it makes of it.
summary: David S. Maynard's Worms? (Electronic Arts, 1983) is built on Paterson's worms, a mathematical game: worms crawl over a grid of points, eating the paths between them. Whenever a worm meets a situation it has never seen, it has to be told which way to go, and from then on it always does the same there. A worm that eats the last path of a point scores it; a worm that reaches a point with no path left dies.

Up to four worms share the grid: taught by players, played by the computer (AUTO), wild (random from the start), or worms taught in earlier games and saved under a name. While no one plays, the computer's worms give a demonstration.
This port follows the Commodore 64 version, translated word by word from its Forth source, which Maynard released under the MIT license. Online, each worm can be a player of its own.

original.author: David S. Maynard (C64 version with Steven Hayes)
original.version: Commodore 64 version ("MASTER OCT. 9, 1983. COMMODORE 64 FINAL", savetz/worms)

controls.action: Start a game (and end the demonstration)
Change the selected worm: none, NEW (taught by a player), AUTO (the computer), WILD, or as it is (its name)
When a worm asks: show the next free path
Take that path; the worm remembers it

controls.input: F1, F3, F5, F7 in a game
controls.action: End the game (F1 starts the program over)

controls.input: L, S, U in the menu
controls.action: Load a worm into the selected one, save it under a name, update its file
The lobby: up to four players, one worm each
